name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that the Pretrial Fairness Act is constitutional and does not unduly infringe on judicial authority, and that the lower court's indefinite detention of the petitioner was unlawful.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred, argued that Spencer's sentence is not a de facto life sentence because he is eligible for parole after 20 years, and Miller v. Alabama does not apply to emerging adults, but Spencer can still bring an as-applied challenge in postconviction proceedings.

name: Justice Hyman
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, arguing Spencer's claim required postconviction proceedings and the majority failed to apply the cruel or degrading standard for proportionate penalties, noting parole eligibility is not the sole factor.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Dissented, argued that the majority should not have denied the motion based on laches and should have addressed the complaint's merits to ensure legislative redistricting plans conform to the Illinois Constitution.

name: Justice Holder White
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: O'BRIEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the police officer's actions constituted an unreasonable warrantless search, and the evidence should have been suppressed.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred with the majority's reasoning and conclusions regarding constitutional violations but dissented on the majority's reliance on the lockstep doctrine, arguing that the court should interpret the Illinois Constitution independently.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that while a blind guilty plea does not waive sentencing claims, the petitioner failed to state a meritorious claim that his 40-year sentence violated the proportionate penalties clause, finding it proportionate to the offense and not shocking the moral sense of the community.

name: Justice Rochford
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that section 1(f) is a statute of repose, section 1.1 applies prospectively, and this application does not violate due process because the defendant's right to a defense accrues when the injury is discovered, not when exposure occurs.

name: Justice Neville
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's opinion legalizes racially discriminatory investigative alerts, permits warrantless arrests in homes without exigent circumstances, misinterprets the Illinois Constitution's warrant requirement, and violates the 2018 consent decree by allowing disparate treatment based on race.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the officer-suit exception applies only to prospective injunctive relief, not to claims for monetary awards to redress past wrongs, which fall under the Court of Claims' jurisdiction.

name: Justice Neville
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the Act does not diminish constitutionally protected pension benefits or constitute a taking of private property.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's exemptions do not violate equal protection or special legislation because plaintiffs are not similarly situated to the exempt classes, and that plaintiffs waived their second amendment and three-readings claims.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Dissented, argued that the Act should be found unconstitutional in its entirety due to a clear violation of the three-readings rule, which undermines constitutional process and democratic norms.

name: JUSTICE OVERSTREET
description: Dissented, argued that the Act should be found unconstitutional in its entirety due to a clear violation of the three-readings rule.

name: JUSTICE O'BRIEN
description: Dissented, argued that the classifications in the legislation do not further its claimed purpose and thus violate the special legislation provision, as the plaintiffs are similarly situated to the exempted groups.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's pretrial release provisions are constitutional and do not violate the bail clause, crime victims' rights clause, or separation of powers clause.

name: Justice O'Brien
description: Concurred, argued that the majority failed to adequately address the defendants' affirmative defense regarding plaintiffs' standing, but ultimately agreed with the constitutionality of the Act.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Dissented, argued that the Act's abolishment of monetary bail directly violates the plain language of the constitution's bill of rights, specifically the vested rights of crime victims, and that the legislature impermissibly usurped the people's sovereign power.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the court's emergency orders tolling the speedy-trial statute were a valid exercise of its constitutional authority over court procedure and did not violate the separation-of-powers clause.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that defendant did not receive ineffective assistance of counsel because his attorney's performance was not deficient and defendant failed to show prejudice, and that the right to be present does not extend to the striking and accepting of jurors.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred, argued that while defendant did not show ineffective assistance, hearings to exercise challenges to jurors do constitute a critical stage of a trial where the defendant has a constitutional right to be present.

name: Justice O'Brien
description: Concurred, argued that counsel was deficient in agreeing to a procedure where defendant was not present for juror challenges, as this is a critical stage, but affirmed because defendant could not establish prejudice.

name: Justice Holder White
description: Concurred, argued that counsel was deficient in agreeing to a procedure where defendant was not present for juror challenges, as this is a critical stage, but affirmed because defendant could not establish prejudice.

name: GARMAN JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the plain language of the safe roads amendment applies to all transportation-related revenues, including those from home-rule units, and that the County's interpretation is unreasonable.

name: JUSTICE THEIS
description: Dissented, argued that the majority failed to harmonize the safe roads amendment with home-rule provisions, and that extrinsic evidence shows the amendment was not intended to limit home-rule units' spending power.

name: OVERSTREET JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the complete failure to swear a jury with a trial oath is a structural error that undermines the integrity of the judicial process and requires automatic reversal, regardless of prejudice.

name: Justice Connors
description: Dissented, argued that the failure to properly swear the jury with a trial oath is a structural error that violates the constitutional right to an impartial jury and requires automatic reversal.

name: GARMAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the City's ordinance definitions were inconsistent with the Act and prior judicial interpretations, and that legislative acquiescence makes judicial construction part of the statute.

name: JUSTICE CARTER
description: Concurred, argued that the appellate court improperly ruled on the proportionate penalties claim without a developed evidentiary record and that the actual innocence claim also needs reconsideration in light of new precedent.

name: Chief Justice Anne M. Burke
description: Concurred in part, dissented in part, argued that the actual innocence claim should be remanded, but the proportionate penalties clause claim is a facial challenge that should be rejected based on Harris without further remand.

name: Justice Michael J. Burke
description: Concurred in part, dissented in part, argued that the actual innocence claim should be remanded, but the appellate court's ruling on the proportionate penalties clause should be reversed outright because the defendant failed to present evidence and the sentencing line is a legislative policy matter.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Concurred in part, dissented in part, argued that the actual innocence claim should be remanded, but the appellate court's ruling on the proportionate penalties clause should be reversed outright because the defendant failed to present evidence and the sentencing line is a legislative policy matter.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Concurred, argued that the post-acquittal computer examination was reasonably directed at obtaining evidence of unauthorized video recording, and the child pornography found was admissible under the plain view doctrine, thus not violating Fourth Amendment rights.

name: Justice Neville
description: Dissented, argued that the search violated McCavitt's constitutional and statutory rights because the warrant was void after 96 hours, and his privacy rights were fully restored upon acquittal, entitling him to the return of his property.

name: THEIS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the firearm and ammunition tax ordinances violate the uniformity clause of the Illinois Constitution because the government failed to establish a substantial relationship between the tax classification and the object of the legislation, especially since it burdens a fundamental right.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's analysis is problematic because it leaves open the possibility for a future, more narrowly tailored tax on firearms and ammunition, which would still violate the Illinois Constitution's provision that the right to bear arms is subject only to police power, not taxation.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE ANNE M. BURKE
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the venue provision is constitutional because the offense of identity theft can be deemed committed where the victim's intangible identifying information is 'located'.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Recused from the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE GARMAN
description: Concurred, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully prolonged, violating the fourth amendment, and therefore Bass's conviction must be reversed and remanded for a new trial, vacating the appellate court's opinion on limited lockstep analysis and investigative alerts.

name: Chief Justice Anne M. Burke
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully extended and the conviction should be reversed, but dissented from vacating the appellate court's holding that defendant's arrest violated article I, section 6 of the Illinois Constitution.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully extended and the conviction should be reversed, but dissented from vacating the appellate court's holding that defendant's arrest was unconstitutional under the warrant clause of the Illinois Constitution, as constitutional review of investigative alerts is merited.
